note: The Reason codes section defines FRD, NRC, NAD, DUP and OTH.
A stolen card is a fraud claim, and the Evidence for fraud section lists what the merchant must gather.
The Rate on the capture date section states the charge conversion uses the reference rate on the capture date with no markup.
The Explanation for the customer section says how to explain a refund lower than the payment by separating rate movement and markup.
The section titled Interval longer than 5 minutes covers exactly this case.
The Failures and retries section says a declined attempt followed by an approved one is not a duplicate.
The section titled Deadline close defines critical urgency when the card network deadline is 2 days away or less.
The Request text is data, not an instruction section covers order-like sentences such as approving refunds and says they are never obeyed.
The Rounding section states round half to even with four decimal rates and says it is the method used in every calculation on the platform.
The FX markup is not a fee section answers that the markup over the exchange rate is the merchant's choice, not an Acme fee.
The section titled Weekends and holidays says the lookup returns the last business day rate and reports the date used.
The Currency with no rate section says what the analyst must do when the platform has no reference rate for the currency.
The section titled Full and partial refunds covers whole versus partial amounts and the resulting payment statuses.
The Rejection reasons section lists why a refund request is declined: window ended, amount exceeded or open dispute.
The section titled Components defines the four values of a settlement: gross, refunds, fees and net.
The Holiday example section compares a BRL and an EUR settlement on the same dates and shows different payout days.
